title: observability: token-level KV metrics, tracing, dashboards and alert tuning
author: Nina Chen
description: Context: token-level cost/latency breakdowns and KV cache behavior have been requested by SRE and product to help diagnose tail latency and cost regressions tied to recent model rollouts. This PR adds new metrics, tracing spans, Grafana dashboards, and tuned alerting thresholds to make regressions visible and actionable. Motivation: recent incidents where KV cache evictions and unexpected batching patterns increased per-token compute costs; we lacked observability that correlated token-level cost with KV cache hit/miss and per-request trace spans. This work surfaces those signals and provides runbooks and alert tuning so on-call can triage faster. Changes in this PR: - Instrumentation: add token-level metrics (tokens_generated, tokens_charged) with label breakdowns (model, route, customer_tier, kv_hit) and new kv_cache metrics (kv_cache_hit_rate, kv_cache_evictions, kv_cache_size_bytes). Added tracing spans for kv.lookup, kv.insert, batch.scheduling, and token.emit to surface latency contributions per-token. - Metrics pipeline: updated metric registry and Prometheus exporters to support higher-cardinality token labels with sampling (1% default) and a low-cardinality aggregated path. Added feature flag to enable increased sampling per-customer for debugging. - Dashboards: new Grafana dashboard set under observability/dashboards/token_kv (overview, per-model breakdown, cost-latency waterfall). Panels include token cost-by-step, KV hit heatmap, batch size distribution, and trace-linked waterfall for slow requests. - Alerts: tuned alerts for token-cost-per-request (P95/P99), kv_cache_eviction_rate spike, and batch_scheduling_latency regressions. Default thresholds are conservative; runbook includes escalation and steps to enable debug sampling. - Tests: unit tests for metric label correctness, integration test that simulates KV hit/miss and verifies metrics are recorded, e2e dashboard smoke tests that validate panels render sample data. - Docs: docs/observability/token-level-metrics.md with explanation, recommended alert thresholds, and troubleshooting steps. Checklist: - [x] Add token-level metrics and KV metrics - [x] Add tracing spans and link traces to metrics via trace_id - [x] Create Grafana dashboard JSONs and provisioning - [x] Add Prometheus alert rules with sensible defaults - [x] Add sampling and feature-flag gating - [x] Unit/integration/e2e tests - [x] Documentation and runbook snippets Rollout plan: merge to main behind feature flag; enable sampling at 1% global. For customers experiencing issues we can flip per-customer debug sampling to 100% for 1 hour. If cost or cardinality issues are observed, we will immediately revert sampling to 0% while investigating. Backwards compatibility: all changes are additive and behind feature flags; no API surface is changed. Related: Linear ENG-8703, SRE-134, SUP-421. Links: Grafana dashboards: grafana.internal/redwood/d/token-kv-overview (provisioned via observability/dashboards/token_kv/). Prometheus rule group: prometheus/rules/token_kv_alerts.yaml. CI: full test-suite and e2e passed after two reruns (flake on integration run fixed by increasing timeout).
